solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nearly a couple of litres in a cask

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, here the litres inside the cask

blocks.note: taken as written
but is a variant spelling of butt, a large cask
two L's, L being the abbreviation for litre

explanation.surface: Someone has drained almost two litres into a barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The two L's go inside A BUT to give ALL BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: All but is an idiom meaning almost or very nearly, as in all but finished.

clue.text: Geordie's behind a historical kidnap

blocks.note: taken as written
hent is an archaic verb meaning to seize or carry off

explanation.surface: A Tyneside man is behind an old abduction.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is someone from Newcastle upon Tyne; AHENT is a northern dialect form of behind.
explanation.definitionFit: In north-east English and Scots dialect, ahent (or ahint) is the regional word for behind or at the back of.

clue.text: For Macron the surges will stop during short month for basic rule

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so these pieces fill up the inside of the surges

blocks.note: la is French for the, Macron being the French president
surges of water are waves
of can mean during, as in of an evening
the abbreviation for October

explanation.surface: A French president vows the waves will stop in a short month, as a basic rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' is easy to read as a container signal, but here it supplies a word: of can mean during, as in of an evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Newlands' law of octaves was an early principle of chemistry, holding that every eighth element repeats properties, hence a basic rule.

clue.text: Rest that is initially bred in need

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows
in says these letters sit inside the word for need

blocks.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
the opening letter of bred
a need is a lack

explanation.surface: Rest, that is, comes first for those bred in poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bred in need' reads as a phrase about upbringing, but in is the container signal and need a separate word.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie back is to recline and relax, which is resting.

clue.text: Territory south of Utah is sound

indicators.note: in a down entry, south of means placed below, so the territory comes after the state

blocks.note: the postal abbreviation for Utah
an abbreviation for territory

explanation.surface: A territory lying south of Utah is in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning healthy; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to voice or pronounce, so it means to sound in the verb sense.

clue.text: Craving? Take in what's nearby, what's most often in bottles

indicators.note: take in reads as the first piece being placed in the second

blocks.note: this is the word used for a thing close at hand
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
T appears twice in bottles, more than any other letter

explanation.surface: Someone with a craving takes in what is nearest and what is most often bottled.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside THIS, then T follows. 'In bottles' seems to mean drink, which suits craving, but it is the letters of the word bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirst is a strong desire or longing, not only for drink, so it is a craving.

clue.text: Turn over a hard bit of safety film

indicators.note: turning something over flips it end to end, so the letters run the other way
a bit of a word is here just its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
sore can mean hard or severe, as in sore trial
the first letter of safety

explanation.surface: An instruction to flip over a tough piece of safety film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safety film' reads as one thing; safety only gives its first letter and film is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A serosa is a serous membrane, a thin protective layer of tissue, so a kind of film.

clue.text: Mug up on grammar — potty, potty

indicators.note: the second potty means crazy, so the letters before it go mad and rearrange

blocks.note: the first potty is the letters to work with

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict that studying grammar is utterly daft.
explanation.walkthrough: Typto, Greek for I strike, was the standard model verb for conjugation drills, so Chambers gives typto as a verb meaning to conjugate.
explanation.definitionFit: To typto is to conjugate the Greek verb, which is swotting up grammar.

clue.text: As icky suet could be!

indicators.note: could be invites another arrangement of the words before it

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An exclamation about how disgusting greasy suet can be.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: icky suet rearranges to the answer, and icky suet is as nasty as can be.
explanation.definitionFit: Icky means sticky and nasty, so suet at its ickiest is the most disgusting, the superlative of yucky.

clue.text: Who'd bend press release involving press?

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: PR stands for press release
to lie heavy on something is to press on it

explanation.surface: A question about who would yield to a press release about the press.
explanation.walkthrough: Press appears twice with different jobs: once inside the abbreviation, once as a verb in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: A plier is one who plies, and to ply in the old sense is to bend or fold.

clue.text: Probe trustee about rank concealing moral quality

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the trustee's letters go round the rest
concealing means hiding inside, so the rank wraps round the moral quality

blocks.note: TR is an abbreviation for trustee
an estate is a social rank or class, as in the three estates
thew, usually plural thews, can mean moral strength or quality

explanation.surface: An inquiry into a trustee's rank and whether it hides good character.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the moral quality sits inside the rank, and both sit inside the trustee abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To test the water is an idiom for trying something out cautiously, which is to probe.

clue.text: Exceptionally large lead weight mostly comprising certain metal

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize
a mouse is a small lead weight used to draw a cord through a gap, as in sash windows

explanation.surface: A huge lead weight is said to be largely made of some metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the metal of the definition, but lead weight is a mouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmous is a chemistry adjective for compounds containing osmium, a specific metallic element.

clue.text: Score for Scots strangely sealed it, huh? League admitted

indicators.note: strangely says the following words are to appear in an odd new order
admitted means let in, so the league letter goes inside

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
L is the abbreviation for league

explanation.surface: A Scottish fan exclaims over a goal that sealed a league game.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots a dule is a goal, so to hail the dules is to score.
explanation.definitionFit: Hail the dules is an old Scots football phrase meaning to put the ball through the goal, i.e. to score.

clue.text: Sheep close to croft — close to hand for Highlanders?

indicators.note: close here means the end, so only the final letter is taken

blocks.note: ewes are female sheep
the final letter of croft

explanation.surface: Sheep near a Scottish smallholding, handy for the Highland folk.
explanation.walkthrough: The first close to means the end of a word; the second is the definition's adjective, near.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewest is a Scots word meaning near or nearby, so close at hand in Highland speech.

clue.text: One from the right thus entering border gets Milesian's characteristic expression

indicators.note: reading from the right means right to left, backwards
entering means going inside the border

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a rim is a border or edge
sic is Latin for thus

explanation.surface: Someone on the political right crosses a border and picks up an Irish turn of phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: Milesians are the legendary ancestors of the Irish, so a Milesian is an Irishman. 'From the right' suggests politics; it means read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iricism is an idiom typical of Irish speech, the same as an Irishism.

clue.text: The enrichment of Tokay, say, is more fine over time

blocks.note: nobler means finer
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A claim that Tokay wine becomes richer and finer as it ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble rot is the Botrytis fungus that shrivels grapes and concentrates their sugar, making sweet wines such as Hungarian Tokay rich.

clue.text: Go on lacking knack?

blocks.note: first meaning: an invitation to help yourself
second meaning, read cryptically: without any feel for something

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a play: someone with no knack has no feel, so they are free of feel, like sugar-free.
explanation.definitionFit: Feel free is an everyday phrase of permission, the same as saying go on, help yourself.

clue.text: I'm with this love of fine arts freshly found in trivium

indicators.note: freshly suggests things made anew, so the letters are set out in a new order

blocks.note: the letters available
these two letters account for part of the word, the remainder being the answer

explanation.surface: A scholar of the medieval arts curriculum claims to have found new love of the fine arts in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits in the middle of the clue, which is rare: I'm plus the answer, mixed up, make the last word. The trivium was the medieval course of grammar, rhetoric and logic.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtu means a taste for or knowledge of fine art objects, a connoisseur's love of the arts.

clue.text: Twisting jest refined chap ripped off good lecturer at Yale, eg

indicators.note: twisting round turns the word so it runs backwards
ripped off means torn away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: to cod is to hoax or joke
a gent is a gentleman
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A gentleman stripped of goodness for a cruel joke at an Ivy League lecturer's expense.
explanation.walkthrough: COD reversed, then GENT without its G.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a docent is a university teacher below professor rank, so a Yale lecturer is an example.

clue.text: As for Hebrews feast starts from Pesah and having Seder

indicators.note: starts means the opening letter of each word that follows

blocks.note: an ale is a rural festival or feast, as in church-ale
the opening letter of Pesah
the opening letter of having
the opening letter of Seder

explanation.surface: A Passover scene: Hebrews feasting at the Seder meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is not a link word but plural letter A's; Pesah is Passover and the Seder its ritual meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, the counterpart of A, so alephs are Hebrew As.

clue.text: Sack servant laid up inside

indicators.note: inside says the second idea sits within the first

blocks.note: a page is a boy servant
laid up means confined to bed by illness

explanation.surface: A servant who was confined to bed is dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' looks like firing the servant; it is the verb to plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, which is what pillage means.

clue.text: With credit blown, biscuits and gravy

indicators.note: something blown is lost or gone, so those letters disappear

blocks.note: crackers are savoury biscuits
CR is the abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: Someone with no credit left is reduced to biscuits and gravy.
explanation.walkthrough: Gravy is slang for easy money, and ackers is British slang for money; biscuits and gravy is a US breakfast dish, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Both ackers and gravy are slang for money, gravy especially for unearned extra cash.

clue.text: Put the wind up aged scold

blocks.note: ae is the abbreviation of aetatis, aged
to rate someone is to scold them

explanation.surface: An elderly nag frightens people.
explanation.walkthrough: To put the wind up someone is to scare them, but read literally it is to blow air into something.
explanation.definitionFit: To aerate is to charge with air, which is literally putting wind into something.

clue.text: Strange case of British bird (6, two words)

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
o' is a short form of of
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: An odd example of a British bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea cob is a dialect name for a seagull, a type of bird.

clue.text: Relieved because Roman gods returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: 'cos is a casual short form of because
dei is Latin for gods

explanation.surface: A sigh of relief because the Roman deities came back.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosy someone is to make them snug and comfortable, so cosied means eased or comforted, relieved.

clue.text: Company check up for space travellers?

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means reading from the bottom, backwards

blocks.note: the abbreviation for company
to stem a flow is to check it

explanation.surface: A firm checks up on astronauts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space travellers' suggests astronauts; the question mark admits the answer is objects, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: Comets are icy bodies that travel through space on long orbits around the sun.

clue.text: Rab C's aim is courage without any hint of manliness

indicators.note: a hint of a word is only its first letter
without means lacking, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: mettle is spirit or courage
the first letter of manliness

explanation.surface: The Glaswegian's aim is to be brave without seeming macho.
explanation.walkthrough: Rab C. Nesbitt is a Glaswegian character from a BBC sitcom, so Rab C's means in Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Ettle is a Scots noun and verb for an intention or aim.

clue.text: Those dabbling in wetlands could be troubled least

indicators.note: troubled means stirred up, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Amateurs dabbling in marsh conservation are the least likely to be bothered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dabbling' suggests amateurs; it describes how dabbling ducks feed at the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Teal are small dabbling ducks that feed in shallow wetland water.

clue.text: Blunt American to flap impatiently

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
in falconry a hawk bates when it flaps its wings to fly off the fist

explanation.surface: A frank American gets agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blunt' looks like an adjective for the American; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate can mean to dull or reduce the force of something, which is to blunt it.

clue.text: Plant one in Scotland around isle

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the Scots word wraps the isle

blocks.note: ane is the Scots word for one
IS is the abbreviation for island or isle

explanation.surface: Someone settles in Scotland on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Ane is the Scots form of one, a convention worth knowing for Scots-flavoured clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Anise is an umbelliferous plant grown for its liquorice-flavoured seeds.

clue.text: Asia's evergreen press chap left article

blocks.note: to jam is to press or squeeze
bo is an American word for a fellow or chap
L is the abbreviation for left
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An Asian journalist stays young, while one man left the article.
explanation.definitionFit: The jambolan is an evergreen tree of the myrtle family native to tropical Asia, also called Java plum.

clue.text: Absent mentor back to whack the gimmes

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the teacher's title is read right to left

blocks.note: A is an abbreviation for absent, as on a register
a rav is a Jewish rabbi or teacher
ice and whack are both slang for kill

explanation.surface: A missing mentor returns to put an end to greedy demands.
explanation.walkthrough: The gimmes, from give me, is slang for greed.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is greed, the urge to have more, which the slang word gimmes captures.

clue.text: What's intrinsic to dramatic fiddle?

indicators.note: what is intrinsic lies within, so the letters sit inside the next word

blocks.note: the letters sit in the middle of this word

explanation.surface: A question about what lies at the heart of a theatrical swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like a cheat; it is a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: An Amati is a violin made by the Amati family of Cremona, makers who taught Stradivari.

clue.text: Grant returning floors housing crib for home office alternatives

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word reads right to left
housing means holding inside, so the floors hold the crib

blocks.note: to let is to allow or grant
étages is French for floors or storeys, also used in English
a crib is a child's cot

explanation.surface: A man called Grant comes back to floors with a cot, setting up a home office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like a man's name; it is the verb. Étages, French for floors, is used in English for storeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Telecottages are rural centres offering shared computer and phone facilities, an alternative to working from a home office.

clue.text: County's essence given the mark of choice?

blocks.note: esse is Latin for being, so essence or existence
a cross is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: The essential character of a county is to be the place people pick.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Essex is one of the home counties of England, bordering London.

clue.text: Stern part that winds up audience

indicators.note: that which winds up a word is its closing letter

blocks.note: to sever is to part or separate
the closing letter of audience

explanation.surface: The serious section of the show that irritates the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winds up' looks like annoys; it means ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and stern both mean strict and harsh in manner.
